title: The minimum on 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 is at the boundary
caption: The unconstrained minimum of (x − 3)² is at x = 3, outside the feasible interval [0, 2]. On the feasible part the curve keeps falling, so the best feasible point is the endpoint x = 2, where f = 1 and the constraint x ≤ 2 is active.
alt: A parabola with minimum at (3, 0), the part with 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 highlighted, and the lowest feasible point (2, 1) marked.
description: The unconstrained minimum is x = 3, where f = 0.
That is infeasible: it breaks x ≤ 2.
On [0, 2] the curve is falling, so moving right always helps until the boundary.
The constrained minimum is f(2) = 1 at x = 2.
